data.name: Lysias
data.long_meaning: A Greek name, Lysias, means Free man. It originates from the Greek words 'lysis' meaning release and 'as' meaning man. In the Bible, Lysias was a Roman officer who helped Paul the Apostle.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizing liberation and freedom in Christ, Lysias inspires individuals to live a life unencumbered by worldly chains.
data.numerology_meaning: As a 6 life path number, Lysias is compassionate, loving, and caring. He is also a natural healer and nurturer, and has a strong desire to help others.

in_hebrew.name: ליסיאס
in_hebrew.meaning: משחרר, מש liberar, לשחרר מן האסורים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ליסיאס הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו 'משחרר' או 'המשחרר'. באסוציאציה נוצרית, השם עשוי להיות קשור לשחרור מן החטא או האסורים הרוחניים. השם מופיע בברית החדשה, בספר מעשי השליחים, כדרגתו של קצין רומי.

in_greek.name: Λυσίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Λυσίας (Lysias) σημαίνει 'ο ἐλευθεριστής' (οἱ ἀπαλλακτής), δηλ. 'αὐτός ὁ ἐλευθερών' ἄνθρωπον ἀπό τινος. Ἄνθρωπος ἱστορικός μέ ἰδιαίτερη σημασία στό βιβλίο τῶν Πράξεων τῶν Αποστόλων.

in_latin.name: Lysias
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Lysias significat 'liberator' vel 'redemptor'. In traditione christiana, nomen hoc potest referri ad liberationem a peccato vel captivitate spirituali. In Actibus Apostolorum, Lysias est tribunus militum Romanorum.

in_english.name: Lysias
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lysias originates from Greek Λυσίας (Lysias), meaning 'liberator' or 'freedom bringer'. It is associated with the concept of release or redemption. In the New Testament, specifically in Acts 21:31-40 and 22:24, Lysias is the name of a Roman tribune who intervenes in the arrest of Paul. The name carries spiritual significance as a symbol of liberation from sin and bondage, resonating with Christian themes of salvation and freedom in Christ.

celebrity_usage: Lysias was the name of an ancient Greek politician, philosopher, and orator, who was a contemporary of Plato and Xenophon.

biblical_reference.note: Lysias is a Roman tribune who intervenes in Paul's arrest.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lysias holds historical significance in the Christian tradition as the Roman officer who helped Paul the Apostle escape from the Roman headquarters in Jerusalem (Acts 21:31-34). Due to Lysias's actions, Paul was able to continue his missionary journeys and spread the gospel to many areas.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Lysias has a spiritual significance as it is a reminder of the freedom and release that comes through faith in God. In the Bible, Paul was a bondservant of Christ (Galatians 1:10) and was set free to spread the word of God to the Gentiles. Similarly, every believer is set free from the bondage of sin and freed to serve God with a joyful heart. The name Lysias symbolizes the liberating power of faith and the hope and freedom that comes from it.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Lysias was an Athenian orator and politician, active in the 4th century BC. The name Lysias carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Lysias continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Peter Lysias in London, United Kingdom credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Lysias, which means "Free man". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Lysias in Greek means "liberator" or "one who looses." In a Christian context, it can symbolize spiritual liberation, freedom from the bondage of sin, and the release of the inner light of God.
